Updated assessment using the May 2017 Beige Book: Conditions across most districts expanded at a modest-to-moderate pace, with widespread employment gains and tightening labor markets; wage pressures were most evident for skilled workers. Housing remained generally solid while commercial real estate was more mixed; tourism activity supported growth, and the energy sector improved. Credit conditions largely mirrored the pace of activity—overall little changed but with tighter standards and terms in riskier pockets (notably auto and some CRE), aligning with the April SLOOS. Price pressures were modest, keeping 12‑month inflation below 2 percent. These Beige Book insights reinforce a cautiously positive outlook consistent with the FOMC’s rate hike and gradual balance‑sheet normalization, while justifying gradualism given below‑target inflation and selective credit tightening.
